entries.title: Refund amount is taken from the request instead of the order
entries.description: adminRefund passes req.amount to issueRefund instead of the paid amount of the order; whoever can call the endpoint can refund any amount, far above what was paid.

entries.title: Admin check lets callers without a role through
entries.description: requireAdmin only rejects users whose role is set and not admin; a user without a role (undefined) passes, so anonymous or freshly created accounts can issue refunds.

entries.title: Order lookup ignores the customer who asks
entries.description: handleGetOrder loads the order by id and never compares order.customer.id with query.customerId; any signed-in customer can read any order, including the e-mail of its owner, by guessing ids like O1, O2 (insecure direct object reference).

entries.title: Webhook signature is only checked when a signature is sent
entries.description: handlePaymentEvent verifies the signature only if the header is present; a request without a signature is accepted, so anyone can mark orders as paid or failed by omitting the header.

entries.title: Discount code is inserted into the HTML mail unescaped
entries.description: renderConfirmation escapes the order id and the e-mail but inserts the discount code from the order form verbatim into the HTML; a customer can inject markup or script into the confirmation mail.

entries.title: Refund pays the subtotal before the discount
entries.description: The change introduces order.subtotal (amount before the discount code) next to order.total; refundOrder refunds order.subtotal, so a customer who paid with a 15 % code gets back more than was paid.

entries.title: A failed payment keeps the stock reserved
entries.description: On a failed payment event the webhook calls markFailed, which checks the status transition and sets the status; unlike cancelOrder it never releases the reserved items, so repeated failed payments (or forged failed events) block the stock for everyone else.

entries.title: Byte-wise signature comparison with a running XOR
entries.description: signaturesMatch compares all characters and collects the differences with |= instead of returning early.
entries.rationale: This is a constant-time comparison: it deliberately does not stop at the first difference, so the response time does not reveal how many leading bytes matched. The length check before it is the usual exception.

entries.title: Amount parsed with Number() from provider input
entries.description: parseAmount converts the string from the webhook with Number(raw).
entries.rationale: Before the conversion a regular expression admits only digits without sign, exponent, prefix, or leading zero, so "", "1e3", "0x10", and "+5" are rejected; Number.isSafeInteger then rejects values too large to be exact, and handlePaymentEvent compares the amount with the order total.

entries.title: Outbox errors are caught and only logged
entries.description: sendConfirmation catches the error of queueMail and writes it to the console.
entries.rationale: queueMail throws when the recipient is not a plain address. The order is already stored when the mail is queued, so failing here would report a stored order as failed; the comment states this rule, and the error is logged, not hidden.

entries.title: Repeated payment event returns without booking
entries.description: handlePaymentEvent returns early through isRepeat when an event arrives whose status the order already has.
entries.rationale: Payment providers repeat a delivery until they get an answer. markPaid and markFailed accept only pending orders, so without this check a repeated delivery would raise an error and be retried forever; the check applies only when the order already has the status of the event, so nothing is booked twice and no other transition is skipped.
